question: There are \(43210\) coins of pairwise distinct weights and three two-pan balances. In one weighing one may choose one of the balances and compare one coin with one other coin. At most one of the three balances is defective; a defective balance may return an arbitrary comparison result, correct or incorrect. What is the minimum number of weighings that guarantees finding the heaviest coin?

The radii of five concentric circles \(\omega_0,\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3,\omega_4\), in this order, form a geometric progression with common ratio \(q>1\). Let \(Q\) be the greatest value of \(q\) for which it is possible to draw a polygonal chain \(A_0A_1A_2A_3A_4\) consisting of four segments of equal length, where \(A_i\in\omega_i\) for every \(i=0,1,2,3,4\). Find \(\lfloor 10000Q\rfloor\).

Let \(n=300\). From unit cubes, \(n^3\) identical \(3\times3\times3\) blocks are made, each block having exactly one black cube at its center and all other unit cubes white. These blocks are assembled into one \(3n\times3n\times3n\) cube. What is the minimum number of white cubes that must be repainted red so that every white cube has at least one common vertex with a red cube?

Let \(k=630\). On an infinite square grid, initially \(N\) cells are marked. The cross of a cell \(A\) is the set of all cells lying in the same row or in the same column as \(A\). If the cross of an unmarked cell \(A\) contains at least \(k\) marked cells, then \(A\) may be marked. What is the least \(N\) for which there exists an initial set of \(N\) marked cells such that, after a sequence of such operations, every cell of the grid can eventually be marked?

A deck has cards whose back sides are all identical, while each front side is colored in one of \(2017\) colors; there are exactly \(10000\) cards of each color. A magician leaves the room. Spectators lay out \(n>1\) cards in a row face up. The assistant sees the row and then turns all cards face down except for one card of his choice, without changing their order. The magician returns, sees the position and color of the card left face up, points to one of the face-down cards, and must correctly name its color. The magician and assistant may agree on a strategy in advance. What is the least \(n\) for which they can guarantee success?

Some cells of a \(200\times200\) square board contain one chip each, either red or blue; the remaining cells are empty. A chip sees another chip if they are in the same row or in the same column. It is known that every chip sees exactly five chips of the other color, and may see any number of chips of its own color. What is the maximum possible total number of chips on the board?

On a \(100\times100\) square grid, several pairwise non-overlapping cardboard right isosceles triangles are placed inside cells. Each triangle is one half of a unit cell, with its two legs lying on two perpendicular unit grid segments of that cell. Every unit grid segment of the board, including boundary segments, is covered by exactly one leg of exactly one triangle. What is the maximum possible number of unit cells that contain no part of any triangle?

For \(n>1\), write the fractions \(\frac1n,\frac2n,\ldots,\frac{n-1}{n}\) in lowest terms, and let \(f(n)\) be the sum of their numerators. For how many integers \(n\) with \(12345\le n\le 98765\) do the numbers \(f(n)\) and \(f(2015n)\) have different parity?

Call a set of \(N\) points in the coordinate plane admissible if their \(x\)-coordinates are pairwise distinct and each point is colored either red or blue. A polynomial \(P(x)\) separates an admissible set if either no red point lies strictly above the graph \(y=P(x)\) and no blue point lies strictly below it, or no blue point lies strictly above the graph and no red point lies strictly below it; points of either color may lie on the graph. For \(N=54321\), find the least integer \(k\) such that every admissible set of \(N\) points can be separated by a polynomial of degree at most \(k\).

Let \(a=233\) and \(b=377\). Some cells of the infinite square grid are marked so that every \(a\times b\) or \(b\times a\) rectangle of grid cells contains at least one marked cell. Let \(\alpha\) be the greatest real number such that for every positive integer \(N\), every such marking contains an \(N\times N\) square with at least \(\alpha N^2\) marked cells. It is known that \(\alpha=1/D\) for an integer \(D\). Find \(D\).

Positive rational numbers \(a\) and \(b\) are written as decimal fractions. The minimal period of each of \(a\) and \(b\) has length \(92032\), while the minimal period of \(a-b\) has length \(46016\). Find the least positive integer \(k\) for which the minimal period of \(a+kb\) can also have length \(46016\).
A positive integer \(n\) is called good if for every positive divisor \(d\mid n\), the number \(d+1\) divides \(n+1\). Find the \(9500\)-th smallest good positive integer.

There are \(54321\) face-down cards on a table, each with a distinct positive integer written on it. In one move, one may point to ten cards and receive one of the ten numbers written on them, without knowing from which of the ten cards it came. What is the largest integer \(t\) such that one can always guarantee identifying \(t\) cards together with the exact numbers written on them?

Let \(n=98765\). For every set of \(n\) points \(A_i=(x_i,y_i)\) in the plane, no three of which lie on one line, and for every choice of real numbers \(c_i\), there exists a real polynomial \(P(x,y)\) of total degree at most \(k\) such that \(P(x_i,y_i)=c_i\) for all \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Find the least possible \(k\).

Let \(P(x)\) be a monic polynomial with real coefficients and degree \(n\). It is possible to choose \(98764\) pairwise distinct real roots \(x_1,\ldots,x_{98764}\) of \(P(x)\) and \(98764\) pairwise distinct real roots \(y_1,\ldots,y_{98764}\) of \(P(x)-1\) such that \(|x_i-y_i|=1\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,98764\). What is the least possible value of \(n\)?

There are \(98765\) pairwise distinct natural numbers greater than \(1\) written on a board. It is known that for every written number \(a\), there are at least \(k\) pairs of written numbers \(b<c\) such that \(bc-1\) is divisible by \(a-1\). What is the greatest possible value of \(k\)?

Let \(a=233\) and \(b=377\). Odd integers \(a\le b\), both greater than \(1\), are fixed. On the square grid, \(2\times2\) square napkins are placed along grid lines so that each unit cell is covered by at most one napkin. It is known that for every \(a\times b\) grid rectangle with horizontal side \(a\) and vertical side \(b\), its lower-left corner is the center of a napkin if and only if its upper-right corner is the center of a napkin. Let \(\alpha\) be the least positive real number such that for every positive integer \(N\), one can always find an \(N\times N\) square containing entirely no more than \(\alpha N^2\) napkins. Write \(\alpha=U/V\) in lowest terms. Find \(V\).
Determine the number of finite nonempty sets \(S\) of positive integers with \(\max S\le54321\) such that for every \(a,b\in S\), there exists \(c\in S\) satisfying \(a\mid b+2c\).

Let \(n=447\). A class of \(n\) students runs \(n\) races, and in every race all students are ranked from \(1\) to \(n\). A student is eligible for a pair of positive integers \((a,b)\) if they finish in the top \(b\) places in at least \(a\) races. The student's final score is the maximum possible value of \(a-b\) over all pairs \((a,b)\) for which they are eligible. What is the maximum possible sum of the final scores of all \(n\) students?

Let \(n\) be a positive even integer. The integers \(1,2,\ldots,n^2\) are to be written in the cells of an \(n\times n\) board, one integer per cell. For every divisor \(d\mid n\), the \(d\)-division of the board is the partition into \((n/d)^2\) nonoverlapping \(d\times d\) subboards. Call \(n\) cool if the integers can be written so that for every divisor \(d\mid n\) with \(1<d<n\), the sum of the integers in every \(d\times d\) subboard of the \(d\)-division is not divisible by \(d\). Find the largest cool even integer \(n\le98765\).

Let \(n=444\). There are \(2n\) knights sitting around a round table, forming \(n\) pairs of partners. Each pair wishes to shake hands, but a pair can shake hands only when its two knights are sitting next to each other. Every minute, one pair of adjacent knights swaps seats. Find the minimum number of adjacent swaps that guarantees that, regardless of the initial arrangement, every knight can meet their partner and shake hands at some time.

Let \(N\) be a positive integer. Geoff and Ceri play a game starting with the integers \(1,2,\ldots,N\) on a board. They alternate moves, with Geoff moving first. On a move, a player chooses a pair of integers \((n,h)\), where \(h>0\) and \(n\) is currently on the board, and then erases every integer \(m\) on the board such that \(2^h\mid |m-n|\). The game continues until the board is empty; the player who erases the last integer loses. For how many integers \(N\) with \(1\le N\le98765\) can Geoff guarantee a win?

Let \(n=24691\). There are \(4n\) marbles with weights \(1,2,\ldots,4n\). James places them on a balance scale so that the total weight on the two sides is equal. Andrew may move one marble from one side to the other, provided that after the move the absolute difference between the total weights of the two sides is at most \(T\). Find the minimum positive integer \(T\) such that Andrew can always make a sequence of legal moves after which every marble is on the opposite side of the scale from where James initially placed it.
Let \(n=444\). Find the minimum possible value of \[S=2^0x_0^2+2^1x_1^2+\cdots+2^nx_n^2,\] where \(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are nonnegative integers satisfying \(x_0+x_1+\cdots+x_n=n\).

Let \(\mathbb Z_{>0}\) be the set of all positive integers. Determine the number of nonempty subsets \(S\subseteq\{2^0,2^1,\ldots,2^{444}\}\) for which there exists a function \(f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}\) such that \[S=\{f(a+b)-f(a)-f(b)\mid a,b\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\}.\]

An infinite sequence \(a_1,a_2,\ldots\) consists of positive integers, each of which has at least three proper divisors. For each \(n\ge1\), the number \(a_{n+1}\) is equal to the sum of the three largest proper divisors of \(a_n\). Among all possible values of \(a_1\), how many are at most \(10^{12}\)? Give the last five digits of this number.

Alice and Bazza play the inequality game with a positive real parameter \(\lambda\). On turn \(n\), starting with \(n=1\), if \(n\) is odd, Alice chooses a nonnegative real number \(x_n\) such that \(x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n\le\lambda n\). If \(n\) is even, Bazza chooses a nonnegative real number \(x_n\) such that \(x_1^2+x_2^2+\cdots+x_n^2\le n\). A player who cannot move loses; if the game continues forever, neither player wins. Let \(\lambda_0\) be the infimum of all \(\lambda\) for which Alice has a winning strategy. Find \(\lfloor 100000\lambda_0\rfloor\).

Consider a \(98765\times98765\) grid of unit squares. Rectangular tiles, possibly of different sizes, may be placed on the grid so that each side of every tile lies on a grid line and every unit square is covered by at most one tile. Determine the minimum number of tiles needed so that each row and each column of the grid has exactly one unit square that is not covered by any tile.

Find the number of periodic sequences \(a_1,a_2,\ldots\) satisfying \[a_{n+2}+a_n^2=a_n+a_{n+1}^2,\qquad |a_{n+1}-a_n|\le1\] for all \(n\ge1\), under the additional condition that every term of the sequence belongs to the set \[\left\{\frac{m}{2025}\ \middle|\ m\in\mathbb Z,\ -24\cdot2025\le m\le24\cdot2025\right\}.\]

A function \(f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}\) is called bonza if \[f(a)\mid b^a-f(b)^{f(a)}\] for all positive integers \(a\) and \(b\). For a positive integer \(n\), let \(v(n)\) be the number of distinct positive integers that can occur as \(f(n)\) for at least one bonza function \(f\). Find \[\sum_{n=1}^{25000}v(n).\]
